holidays.name: National Jerky Day
holidays.description: A day for tearing into the chewiest, most portable snack there is. Beef, turkey, venison, salmon and even plant-based jerky all get their moment. Pack a bag for a road trip, a hike, or the office drawer.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance created by snack fans. Its exact founder is unclear, and it has become a yearly staple on June 12.
holidays.funFact: The word jerky comes from the Quechua word ch'arki, meaning dried, salted meat. The Andean Quechua people were drying meat this way centuries before modern snack aisles existed.

holidays.name: Loving Day
holidays.description: A celebration of love without legal barriers, honoring the end of laws that banned interracial marriage in the United States. People mark it with picnics, festivals, and storytelling about the couple behind the case.
holidays.origin: It commemorates June 12, 1967, when the U.S. Supreme Court decided Loving v. Virginia. The ruling struck down state bans on interracial marriage. Richard and Mildred Loving had been convicted in Virginia for marrying each other. The day was later popularized as an annual celebration by grassroots organizers.
holidays.funFact: The case was named for the plaintiffs' surname, Loving. It is probably the most fitting name in Supreme Court history.

holidays.name: National Peanut Butter Cookie Day
holidays.description: A salute to the crisscross-fork-marked classic, with its crumbly, nutty, sweet goodness. Bakers go for chewy, crispy, or flourless versions, and some press a chocolate kiss into the center.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday of unclear origin. Cookie fans have kept it going on June 12 as a reason to bake.
holidays.funFact: The famous fork crisscross pattern has a practical purpose. Peanut butter dough is dense, so pressing it flat helps the cookies bake evenly.
